proofUses.reason: For a continuous generating trace, the terminal domain-boundary distance equals distance to the full trace and the real line. A swallowed component cannot be entered by the future trace. Trace existence and hull generation remain explicit inputs.
The radius tail bound and positive hypergeometric moment bound become uniform on compact subsets of H. For kappa at least eight the trace-distance consequence is stated for each fixed point.

Separate outer and inner grids prove the covering estimates without a boundary-localization error. The available lower bound at every scale gives a full logarithmic limit, strengthening the source limsup; trace generation remains assumed.

Dyadic covers and a summable expected q-cost give zero Hausdorff q-measure above one plus kappa over eight. A countable interior exhaustion and the real-line bound handle the whole trace; no lower dimension bound is inferred.

The deterministic boundary inclusion in the past trace plus the real line transfers the full-trace dimension bound to all times on one event. This includes kappa four and gives zero area without the separate Holder-domain boundary theorem; no optimal hull-boundary exponent is claimed.
